name: TV DIABLO Windows
note: v3376: Your second eye said VERDICT: clean and the ledger recorded that it found four defects. MEASURED LIVE on v3375 own look, minutes after the ship: the answer FIRST LINE was literally VERDICT: clean, and the row came back verdict=findings with findings=4 - every one of them the answer explaining WHY it is clean, finding [0] containing the words VERDICT: clean inside itself. That matters because agreement() reads verdicts, so a misread look is laundered straight into the confluence figures the heart reports. THE ROOT CAUSE IS AN UNJOINED END INSIDE MY OWN INSTRUMENT. _declares_none knows two shapes, the NOUN PHRASE (no concrete defects found) and the PRONOUN (none found), and has never known the ADJECTIVE the ledger itself uses. The ledger vocabulary is clean | findings | cannot-tell, the review prompt asks the eye to answer in exactly that vocabulary, and the parser did not know the word. Three parts, two agreed, one did not. Sixth phrasing to defeat this check - #67 was the fifth at v3315. THE FIX READS A DECLARED FIELD, NOT PROSE, AND THAT DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE SAFETY. #76 measured that widening _declares_none cannot be made safe, and #117 measured that a bullet filter would EAT A REAL FINDING. So _stated_verdict reads a line that STATES the verdict, anchored at line start, in the ledger own vocabulary; prose is never consulted. A MENU IS NOT A DECLARATION: the review prompt itself contains the line 1. VERDICT: clean / findings, so any line naming two or more verdict words is ignored and the parser falls back to the prose path unchanged. AND A STATED CLEAN STILL CANNOT CLEAR A REAL CLAIM - the existing _claims_a_defect refusal runs first, so reading the field can never become an off switch. Verified by RUNNING all four shapes: the real v3375 answer -> clean, a stated findings -> findings, the prompt echo -> no declaration, a stated clean beside a P1 crash and a race -> findings. PARSER_GEN v3315 -> v3376 so every row still says which parser judged it. 11 cases, 6 red-proofs PROVEN. WARNING ONE RED-PROOF CAME BACK BLIND AT A CORRECT MATCH COUNT OF 1 AND THE SABOTAGE WAS RIGHT. My menu case used the NUMBERED form 1. VERDICT: clean / findings - the form the prompt actually uses - and measured it never matches the line anchor at all, because a leading 1. is not in the character class. It returned None for a reason unrelated to the menu guard, so the CASE could not see the sabotage. Split into two cases: the bare menu reaches the guard, the numbered form is stopped by the anchor, and each is a different door. HEART - verdict matches the answer, in CHECKS, MINE, WATCHES and NO_JOINT_YET. Two independent sides: our parser verdict against the other family own stated words, re-read from answerHead. WARNING MY FIRST CUT OF THIS ROW WAS WRONG AND I CAUGHT IT BEFORE SHIPPING: unscoped, it reported 118 rows that verdict_provenance() ALREADY counts - it reports 331 re-judgeable, 213 agree, 118 do not - which is one reader wearing two names. v3375 carries judgedBy=v3315 and is exactly one of that 118, so it is re-judgement DEBT belonging to that reader, not a live break. The row is now scoped to the CURRENT generation and asks what nothing else asks: has the parser running right now written a row its own answer denies. It reads UNKNOWN today because no v3376-judged row exists yet, and UNKNOWN is never OK. v3375 ROW IS DELIBERATELY NOT REWRITTEN. Rows are immutable and verdict_provenance() re-judges on read; rewriting history to make a heart row green is the opposite of the point.
